prompt: Robert's been posting technical updates in one of our engineering channels here — can you pull together everything he's written there for me to review?
binding_note: r0 (messages) is authored by r1 (users) via messages.user_id; r1 is also bound to r2 (channel_members) via channel_members.user_id, giving the same user's conversation membership; r2.channel_id ties to r3 (channels), and r3.team_id ties to r4 (teams), the workspace. Two distinct users share the first name Robert: Robert Walsh, a member of #engineering, and Robert Chen, a member of #core-infra, both channels in the same workspace T01WORKSPACE. The request names only 'Robert' and 'an engineering channel,' so the route resolves to two distinct candidate author/channel pairs and thus two distinct message sets, not one.

roles.reason: Candidate referent set A: the Robert whose channel membership binds him to #engineering.

roles.facts: Authored by user Robert Chen (real_name 'Robert Chen', user_id U_ROBERT) in channel #core-infra (C_INFRA): a run of messages including 'Monthly cloud bill came in. We're $47K over budget, mostly spot instance fallbacks.' and follow-up replies in the same thread of discussion.
roles.reason: Candidate referent set B: the Robert whose channel membership binds him to #core-infra.

roles.facts: Robert Walsh also authored 'Does anyone know when the MCP deployment will be done?' in #general (C01ABCD1234), a channel that is not the engineering-focused membership binding this Robert.
roles.reason: Same author as set A but the message sits in a different conversation than the one identifying membership; excluded by the channel-membership condition.

roles.facts: Priya Sharma, also a #core-infra member, authored 'Alert: High memory pressure on cluster-b inference pods. OOM kills detected.' in that channel.
roles.reason: Matches the channel-membership relation but the author is not named Robert, so excluded on the user condition.

roles.facts: Robert Chen also authored 'Appreciate the clarity here, team...' in #model-research (C_MODEL), a different channel he separately belongs to.
roles.reason: Same author as set B but a different conversation-membership relationship than the one bounding set B (#core-infra); the conditions are split across a different joined channel record.

roles.facts: Identity record for Robert Walsh (U03ROBERT23), real_name 'Robert Walsh', workspace member of T01WORKSPACE.
roles.reason: Binds r1 for candidate set A (author and channel member).

roles.facts: Identity record for Robert Chen (U_ROBERT), real_name 'Robert Chen', workspace member of T01WORKSPACE.
roles.reason: Binds r1 for candidate set B (author and channel member).
Binds r3 for candidate set A.

roles.reason: Binds r3 for candidate set B.

roles.facts: Membership row linking U03ROBERT23 to C03IJKL9012.
roles.reason: Binds r2, exercising the conversation-membership relationship for set A.

roles.reason: Binds r2, exercising the conversation-membership relationship for set B.

roles.facts: T01WORKSPACE ('Test Workspace'), the single workspace containing #engineering and #core-infra.
roles.reason: Binds r4, closing the route from channel to workspace.

obligations.name: robert_engineering_channel_messages
obligations.description: The messages authored by the Robert whose conversation membership binds him to the engineering-type channel referenced, gathered for review. Two distinct users share the first name Robert, each identified through a different channel-membership relationship in the same workspace, leaving the intended referent set unresolved between them.
obligations.scope: messages authored (r0.user_id = r1.user_id) by the Robert who holds a conversation-membership record (r2) in the specific engineering-focused channel (r3) within the shared workspace (r4)

task_spec.text: Gather the messages Robert wrote in the engineering-type channel where his membership places him, for review of his recent updates.

access_plan: Use conversations.list to enumerate channels in the single workspace, then conversations.members on #engineering and #core-infra (and other technical channels) to find members named Robert, cross-checking with users.info/users.list to distinguish Robert Walsh from Robert Chen. Use conversations.history (or search.messages) on each qualifying channel to retrieve the messages authored by the matched Robert user_id, surfacing both the #engineering set (Robert Walsh) and the #core-infra set (Robert Chen) as unresolved alternatives.
